questions.question:
위 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것을 두 개 고르면?

ⓐEnglish has some words which have borrowed from other cultures or languages. Here are some examples with interesting stories.

shampoo
The word shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo, which means "to press." In India, the word was used for a head massage. ⓑBritish traders in India experienced a bath with a head massage, and it was introduced to Britain by them in the 18th century. The meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times after it first entered English around 1762. In the 19th century, shampoo got its present meaning of "washing the hair." ⓒShortly after getting that meaning, the word began to be also used for a special soap for the hair.

robot

ⓓThe word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which is written in 1920 by a Czech writer, Karel Čapek. In the play, robots are machines that look like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory.

ⓔIt is interesting that Karel Čapek himself didn't think of the idea of using the word robot. He originally called the machines in his play labori from the Latin word for "work." However, his brother suggested roboti, which means "slave workers" in Czech. Karel Čapek liked the idea and decided to use the word roboti. In 1938, the play was made into a science fiction show on television in Britain.
questions.explanation:
ⓐ 'English has some words which have borrowed'는 'have'가 주동사인데 'borrowed'는 과거분사이므로 어색함. 'English has some words which have been borrowed' 또는 'English has some words borrowed'가 맞음.

ⓓ 'which is written in 1920'은 주어진 시간이 과거이므로 'which was written in 1920'이 맞음.

ⓑ, ⓒ, ⓔ는 문법적으로 올바름.

options: The word shampoo means "to press" in Britain.
The meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times before 1762.
The word shampoo got the meaning of "washing the hair" right before it got the meaning of "a special soap for the hair."
Karel Čapek liked his brother's idea and decided to use the Latin word roboti, which means "slave workers."
The word labori was used in a science fiction show in 1938.

questions.question:
다음 글을 읽고 답할 수 없는 질문은?

The word hurricane comes from the Spanish word huracán, which originates from the name of a Mayan god. In the Mayan creation myth, Huracán is the weather god of wind, storm, and fire, and he is one of the three gods who created humans. However, the first humans angered the gods, so Huracán caused a great flood.

The first Spanish contact with the Mayan civilization was in 1517. Spanish explorers who were passing through the Caribbean experienced a hurricane and picked up the word for it from the people in the area. In English, one of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare in 1608.
questions.explanation:
⑤ "one of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare in 1608"이라고 했으므로, 몇 번 사용되었는지(how many times)는 글에서 알 수 없음. 글은 Shakespeare의 작품에서 한 번 이상 사용되었다는 것만 알려줌.

① Huracán은 마야 신화의 날씨의 신
② 글에서 '세 명의 신'이라고 명시
③ 인간들이 신들을 화나게 해서
④ 허리케인을 경험함

The meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times after ⓒit first entered English around 1762. In the 19th century, shampoo ⓓgot their present meaning of "washing the hair." Shortly after that, the word ⓔbegan to also use for a special soap for the hair.

The word hamburger originally comes from Hamburg, Germany's second-largest city. Hamburger means "people or things from Hamburg" in German.

The origin of the first hamburger is not clear. However, it is believed ⓕthat the hamburger was invented in a small town in Texas, USA, sometime between 1885 and 1904. ⓖA cook was placed a Hamburg-style steak between two slices of bread, and people started to call such food a hamburger.
questions.explanation:
ⓐ Here are some examples = 올바름 (examples가 복수이므로 are)
ⓒ it first entered = 올바름 (시간적 순서)

어법상 틀린 것:
ⓑ introduced it Britain = introduced it to Britain (전치사 to 필요)
ⓓ got their = got its (their는 복수, its가 맞음)
ⓔ began to also use = began to be also used (수동형 필요)
ⓖ was placed = was placed (능동형이면 'A cook placed' 또는 수동형이면 '문장 구조 재정의' 필요. 아마도 'placed'가 맞음)

ⓐEnglish has often borrow words from other cultures or languages. Here are some examples with interesting stories.

The word shampoo comes from the Hindi word chāmpo, which means "to press." ⓑIn India, the word was used for a head massage. British traders in India experienced a bath with a head massage and introduced it to Britain in the 18th century.

The meaning of the word shampoo changed a few times ⓒafter it first entered English around 1762. In the 19th century, shampoo got its present meaning of "washing the hair." Shortly after that, the word began to be also used for a special soap for the hair.

The word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which was written in 1920 by a Czech writer, Karel Čapek. In the play, ⓓrobots are machines that looks like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory.

It is interesting that the idea of using the word robot didn't come from Karel Čapek himself. He originally called the machines in his play labori from the Latin word for "work." However, his brother suggested roboti, which means "slave workers" in Czech. ⓔKarel Čapek liked the idea and decided using the word roboti. In 1938, the play was made into a science fiction show on television in Britain.

위 글의 밑줄 친 (A)의 우리말을 알맞게 영작한 것은?

(A)Hamburger는 1885년에서 1904년 사이의 언젠가 미국의 텍사스에 있는 작은 마을에서 발명되었다고 믿어진다.
questions.explanation:
"~라고 믿어진다"는 "it is believed that ~"로 표현하고, 발명된 것은 과거이므로 "was invented"를 써야 함.

③ "it is believed that the hamburger was invented in a small town in Texas, USA, sometime between 1885 and 1904"가 정확한 영작

① is invented는 현재 수동형으로 부정확 (시간이 과거)
② to be invented는 부정사로 주어 역할을 하는데, 'believed to be invented'는 의미가 다름
④ 주어-동사 일치 오류와 문법 오류
⑤ 완전히 잘못된 문장 구조

questions.question:
다음 글의 밑줄 친 ⓐ~ⓔ 중, 어법상 어색한 것은?

The word robot comes from the play R.U.R., which was written in 1920 by a Czech writer, Karel Čapek. In the play, robots are machines ⓐthat look like humans. They are designed to work for humans and are produced in a factory.

In 1938, the play was ⓔmade into a science fiction show on television in Britain.
questions.explanation:
ⓐ that look like humans = 올바름
ⓑ using the word robot = 올바름 (동명사)
ⓒ that means = which means (주격 관계대명사로 선행사가 roboti인데, 제한적 용법이면 that 또는 which 모두 가능하지만, 계속적 용법이 되려면 which만 가능. 여기서는 쉼표가 없으므로 제한적 용법이고 both가능하지만, 문맥상 which가 더 자연스러움. 그런데 that을 쓴 것도 문법적으로 가능하므로...) - 실제로는 which를 쓰는 것이 더 적절

그런데 다시 보니, "roboti, that means"의 구조에서 쉼표 뒤에 that을 쓰는 것은 계속적 용법인데 계속적 용법에서는 that을 쓸 수 없고 which를 써야 함.

ⓓ decided to use = 올바름
ⓔ made into = 올바름

③ ⓒ이 어법상 어색함. that → which

options: (A): lent

questions.question:
다음 글의 빈칸 (A)~(E)에 들어갈 말로 알맞게 연결된 것은?

English has often (A)__________ words from other cultures or languages. Here is an example with an interesting story.

The word hamburger (B)__________ comes from Hamburg, Germany's second-largest city. Hamburger means "people or things from Hamburg" in German.

The origin of the first hamburger is not (C)__________. However, it is believed that the hamburger was invented in a small town in Texas, USA, (D)__________ between 1885 (E)__________ 1904. A cook placed a Hamburg-style steak between two slices of bread, and people started to call such food a hamburger.
questions.explanation:
각 빈칸의 올바른 단어:

(A) borrowed (English has often borrowed words) - lent는 아님
(B) originally (The word hamburger originally comes from) - origin은 아님 (명사)
(C) clear (The origin is not clear) - 선택지 ③ 정답
(D) sometime (sometime between 1885) - sometimes가 아님
(E) and (between 1885 and 1904) - or가 아님

① (A): lent - 틀림 (borrowed 필요)
② (B): origin - 틀림 (originally 필요)
③ (C): clear - 맞음
④ (D): sometimes - 틀림 (sometime 필요, 하나의 시간 지점)
⑤ (E): or - 틀림 (and 필요)

questions.question:
다음 글과 일치하는 것을 두 개 고르면?

The word hurricane comes from the Spanish word huracán, which originates from the name of a Mayan god. In the Mayan creation myth, Huracán is the weather god of wind, storm, and fire, and he is one of the three gods who created humans. However, the first humans angered the gods, so Huracán caused a great flood.

The first Spanish contact with the Mayan civilization was in 1517. Spanish explorers who were passing through the Caribbean experienced a hurricane and picked up the word for it from the people in the area. In English, one of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare in 1608.
questions.explanation:
① "The Spanish word huracán comes from the name of a Mayan god" - 글에서 "the Spanish word huracán, which originates from the name of a Mayan god"라고 명시됨. ✓

② "Huracán, the weather god, created humans all by himself" - 글에서 "he is one of the three gods who created humans"이라고 했으므로 혼자가 아님. ✗

③ "Huracán caused a great earthquake" - 글에서는 "great flood"이라고 했지 earthquake가 아님. ✗

④ "The Mayan civilization was destroyed" - 글에서 이런 내용이 없음. ✗

⑤ "The English word hurricane was used in one of shakespeare's plays" - "In English, one of the early uses of hurricane was in a play by Shakespeare in 1608"에서 확인됨. ✓
